shortQuestions: The world sees Pakistan as a country of great tourism potential: international travel magazines and agencies have ranked it among the best adventure and holiday destinations because of its mountains, history, culture and hospitality, although security concerns and poor facilities have kept tourist numbers low.

Natural attractions include the world's highest mountains (K-2, Nanga Parbat) and the Karakoram, Himalaya and Hindu Kush ranges; glaciers (Baltoro, Siachen); valleys like Swat, Kaghan, Hunza, Skardu and Chitral; lakes (Saiful Muluk, Attabad); deserts (Thar, Cholistan); and beaches of Makran and Karachi.

The Karakoram Highway follows part of the ancient Silk Route that linked China with South Asia and the West. Built jointly by Pakistan and China, it is one of the highest paved roads in the world and is called the 'Eighth Wonder of the World'; it is historically and economically important as a link between the two countries (and CPEC).

Religious sites: for Muslims — the Badshahi Mosque, Faisal Mosque, shrines of Data Ganj Bakhsh and other saints; for Sikhs — Gurdwara Nankana Sahib (birthplace of Guru Nanak), Kartarpur and Panja Sahib; for Buddhists — Taxila, Takht-i-Bahi and Swat's stupas; for Hindus — Katas Raj and Hinglaj. They are significant as centres of faith, history and interfaith harmony.

Balochistan has the beautiful Makran coast and beaches (Gwadar, Kund Malir, Ormara), the Hingol National Park and Princess of Hope rock, Ziarat's juniper forests and Quaid's Residency, the ancient site of Mehrgarh, unique deserts and mountains — making it rich in natural and historical tourism.

We can improve Pakistan's image by ensuring security for tourists, building roads, hotels and facilities, easy online visas, promoting Pakistan on international media and social media, hosting international events, training tour guides, keeping sites clean, and showing our hospitality and culture to the world.

For Buddhists Pakistan holds the heritage of the Gandhara civilisation — Taxila, Takht-i-Bahi, Swat valley and Peshawar Museum with famous Buddha statues and stupas. For Sikhs it has their holiest places — Nankana Sahib, Kartarpur (connected by the Kartarpur Corridor), Panja Sahib at Hasan Abdal and Gurdwara Dera Sahib in Lahore. Religious tourism can attract millions of pilgrims.
activities: Sample description — A Visit to Taxila: (Introduction with central idea) My visit to Taxila showed me how rich Pakistan's ancient heritage is. (Body) Last spring our class visited the Taxila Museum and the ruins of Sirkap and Dharmarajika. In the museum we saw stone statues of the Buddha, coins and jewellery of the Gandhara period. At Sirkap we walked along the ancient streets and saw the remains of houses and temples. The guide explained that Taxila was a great centre of learning 2,500 years ago. (Conclusion) The trip made me proud of our history and convinced me that such sites must be preserved and shown to the world.

Speaking game guide: each student writes two true statements and one false statement about himself (e.g., "I have climbed Mount Elum", "I can play the flute", "I have three sisters"); classmates ask questions to find the false one. It practises asking questions, listening and speaking confidently.
